Please be careful with the Diamond Way by Ole Nydahl. He is a living controversial issue. I haven't heard of sex scandals but of structures that come close to ones used by sects. Like: "You don't meet and talk to other buddhists. They can't teach you like we do." They don't use original writings about the dharma. They use writings by Ole Nydahl, which is unauthentic. They have different names for divinities every other school uses. And the list goes on. You could go an visit them. But keep in mind that there are disputes. Another "school" you will easily find is the NKT (new kadampa tradition). They ARE a sect. Be careful there as well. Since i don't know in which region you are looking for a buddhist community i can only ask you to listen to your heart and your common sense. Other problems are Ole Nydals disparaging attitude towards Islam, his political statements, his manner of expressing and presenting himself, and his relationships with women. Altogether he and his organisation act pretty much unbuddhistic in the eyes of many people. And i agree with them. But in the end i don't care too much about the inner-buddhist-politics. And i really feel sorry for people who develop ambitions of power within a philosophy that teaches the opposite. TLDR: Yes, his Lama-title is accepted. But: Yes, seemingly to keep up the show.
